column1: # 10장 말투 지시. 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명. 장부·일기(@letter)는 지시하지 않는다.
@scene 일요일 아침 열한 시, 나는 혼자
column2: Sunday, eleven o'clock, Yuna sits alone on the steps of Santa Maria del Mar, the time and place of the old letter. Bells ring. Vale phones and invites her to the beach, using the Argentine command "vení" (in Spain it would be "ven"). Quiet, then lightly pulled into the day.

column1: 일요일 아침 열한 시, 나는 혼자

column2: quick and cheerful on the phone, insisting

Barceloneta beach with Vale's friends: Luca from Italy, Sofía from Mexico, Pau from Barcelona, each speaking a different Spanish. They argue playfully about what is "más ... que" or "menos ... que" in their home countries; Yuna learns comparisons and adds her own about Korea. Sunny, friendly.
warm Mexican greeting, a friendly question

column1: Il sole… el sol de Barcelona
column2: slow, starting in Italian then switching; stress "más fuerte que"
friendly, inviting her in, a real question

column1: En Corea, el café es más caro
column2: slow and careful, a beginner; a small smile on the last part about pan con tomate

At the beach Yuna lies in the sun for the first time in ages and gets badly sunburnt. Sofía shouts when she sees her red back. Yuna learns "me duele" (like "me gusta", the thing that hurts is the subject) and the friends take care of her. Comic and warm.

column1: 나는 수건 위에 누워 하늘을 보았다

column2: wincing, a beginner, finding the words

Late afternoon. Marc, reserved, arrives at the beach with the ledger; Montse told him where Yuna was, and Vale's friends exchange knowing looks. In the ledger he found an address for "S." in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. Yuna remembers her grandmother once spoke of an island far away, and that her mother may have been born there. Quiet discovery, then a light joke from Vale.

column1: He leído más. En el libro
Está en una isla. Gran Canaria
Mi abuela… vive en una isla
